title: Piecewise Function Evaluation and Boundary Analysis
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement:
Consider the piecewise-defined function:
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x + 1, & x < 1 \\ 4 - x^2, & 1 \le x \le 3 \\ -5, & x > 3 \end{cases}$$
Evaluate the function values f(0), f(1), f(2), and f(3), and determine whether the function agrees at the transition boundaries x = 1 and x = 3.
hints: Check which domain sub-interval contains each given input before selecting which rule to evaluate.
Pay close attention to whether boundary inequalities are inclusive (<=) or strict (<).
At x = 1, compare the limit from the left rule 2x + 1 with the value assigned by the inclusive middle rule 4 - x^2.
finalAnswer: f(0) = 1, f(1) = 3, f(2) = 0, f(3) = -5; function values agree continuously across both boundary transitions

steps.title: Evaluate f(0)
steps.explanation: Since 0 is strictly less than 1, the first rule 2x + 1 applies, yielding f(0) = 1.
steps.why: Each input in a piecewise function must be evaluated strictly using the formula assigned to its specific domain partition.

steps.title: Evaluate f(1) at the First Boundary
steps.explanation: The condition 1 <= x <= 3 includes x = 1, so the middle rule governs this point: f(1) = 4 - 1 = 3. Notice also that the left branch approaches 2(1) + 1 = 3, matching seamlessly.
steps.why: Inclusive inequalities determine ownership of the boundary point for piecewise evaluation.

steps.title: Evaluate f(2) in the Interior Interval
steps.why: The input 2 satisfies 1 <= 2 <= 3, matching the middle quadratic rule.

steps.title: Evaluate f(3) at the Second Boundary
steps.explanation: The point x = 3 is included in the middle branch, giving f(3) = 4 - 9 = -5. For x > 3, the third branch is constant at -5, so both branches agree at the junction.
steps.why: When the one-sided limits from adjacent branches match the function value at a boundary, the graph joins without a jump.
